nativeOutcome: One additional participant below the study's 3-item UCLA loneliness threshold at six months
decision: Do not publish a dollars-per-10-QALYs price. The IOA pilot measured a binary 3-item UCLA loneliness threshold, not preference-based health utility, and its 46%-to-28% change came from an uncontrolled cohort with substantial loss to follow-up. Available utility studies are cross-sectional, use different loneliness definitions and health-utility instruments, and do not establish the timing or persistence of a utility gain.

candidateEvidence.design: Systematic review of 19 observational studies reporting loneliness or social isolation alongside health-state utility values
candidateEvidence.population: People with pre-existing health conditions; populations, conditions, loneliness measures, and utility instruments varied
candidateEvidence.contrast: Lonely versus not lonely in two chronic-condition studies using HUI2 or EQ-5D-3L
candidateEvidence.boundary: The 0.04 difference is a cross-sectional association in other populations, not a causal effect of Friendship Line, a mapping from the 3-item UCLA threshold, or a measured six-month utility gain. The review found heterogeneity and confounding too substantial for quantitative synthesis.

failedGates.label: Map the loneliness threshold to utility
failedGates.why: The IOA study defined loneliness as 3 or more points on the 3-item UCLA scale. The candidate utility literature used varied loneliness definitions and preference-based instruments; no validated mapping from this binary threshold to EQ-5D, HUI, SF-6D, or AQoL utility was located.

failedGates.label: Separate loneliness from correlated illness
failedGates.why: The 0.04 utility gap is observational and comes from people with pre-existing health conditions. Depression, disability, chronic illness, and other confounding can affect both loneliness and utility, so the association cannot be treated as the causal utility gained by remitting loneliness.

failedGates.label: Measure Friendship Line's causal effect
failedGates.why: The pilot had no concurrent control group. Of 175 baseline participants, 121 had any follow-up and only 78 completed the six-month interview; regression to the mean, secular change, selection, and missing outcomes remain unresolved.

failedGates.label: Establish timing and persistence
failedGates.why: A lower loneliness share at six months does not establish when a change began, its area under the curve, whether it persisted after the final interview, or whether health utility changed for the same duration.

failedGates.label: Choose a defensible utility instrument
failedGates.why: The evidence review warns that EQ-5D may be insufficiently sensitive to psychological and social outcomes and that different instruments can yield materially different values. IOA did not directly collect a preference-based utility measure.

illustrativeCounterfactual.assumptions: If, contrary to the missing evidence, each modeled six-month remission caused the full 0.04 annual utility difference for exactly six months, assign 0.02 QALY per remission.
illustrativeCounterfactual.publicationBoundary: This arithmetic is shown only to expose the unsupported mapping, causality, and duration assumptions. It must not appear as IOA's comparison price, rank, or recommendation.

requiredEvidence: Pre-specify the 3-item UCLA outcome and collect a preference-based utility measure at baseline, intermediate time points, and follow-up.
Use a randomized or credible concurrent comparison with complete participant flow, exposure, missing-data analysis, and a pre-specified causal estimand.
Estimate the utility change jointly with loneliness so the bridge does not rely on a cross-study threshold mapping.
Measure onset, area under the utility curve, and persistence beyond the six-month endpoint.
Publish incremental Friendship Line cost, payer and public-funding displacement, capacity, and a dated marginal funding plan.
